title: Fix per-memory Suppress/Unblock targeting all memories and broken duration until_tick math

sections.what: Fix per-memory Suppress and Unblock across mind-view.ts, memory-view.ts, routes/memories.py, and player.py so suppressing one memory targets only that entryId and computes until_tick relative to current_tick.
sections.why: In static/js/inspector/mind-view.ts (lines 351-352), per-memory Suppress/Unblock buttons pass (charName, mid), but static/js/inspector/memory-view.ts (lines 300-310, 562) ignores entryId and sends { tags: [], duration: 1 } / {}. Meanwhile routes/memories.py (lines 1257-1280) has no memory_id parameter, and player.py (lines 1508, 1529) includes `or (not tags and not keywords_lower):` which matches every memory in player.memories. In addition, player.py line 1510 stores `until_tick = duration` directly (1) without adding current_tick, so any non-zero tick treats timed suppressions as already expired in is_active_memory and clear_expired_suppressions.
sections.how:
1. Update routes/memories.py (/api/players/<name>/memories/suppress and /unblock) and Player.suppress_memory / Player.unblock_memory in player.py to accept an optional memory_id (or memory_ids), and remove the silent empty-filter wildcard fallback (or (not tags and not keywords_lower):) unless an explicit all=true / wildcard flag is passed.
2. Pass world tick into Player.suppress_memory so positive duration computes until_tick = current_tick + duration instead of raw duration, while preserving duration <= 0 -> None for permanent suppressions.
3. Update static/js/inspector/memory-view.ts (suppressMemory lines 300-304, unblockMemory lines 306-310, and editor modal line 562) plus ApiClient wrappers to forward entryId as memory_id and allow choosing a turn duration cleanly.
4. Add Python and JS unit tests covering single-ID suppress/unblock isolation, empty-filter safety, and positive-duration expiry across ticks > 1.
sections.verify:
1. Run pytest memory suppression tests at current_tick=20 asserting suppressing entry A with duration=3 sets until_tick=23, leaves entry B active, and empty tags/keywords without wildcard flag suppresses 0 entries.
2. Run npm run build:ts and JS unit tests for InspectorMemory.suppressMemory / unblockMemory asserting entryId is forwarded as memory_id.

acceptance.text: InspectorMemory.suppressMemory(charName, entryId) and unblockMemory(charName, entryId) pass entryId/memory_id so only the clicked memory card is suppressed or unblocked.
routes/memories.py (/suppress, /unblock) and Player.suppress_memory/unblock_memory support explicit memory_id targeting and reject empty wildcard calls unless an explicit wildcard flag is supplied.

Player.suppress_memory stores until_tick = current_tick + duration when duration > 0 (leaving duration == 0 as permanent None) and unit tests verify duration > 0 survives through clear_expired_suppressions and is_active_memory across non-zero ticks.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Character Inspector -> Mind -> Memories list (static/js/inspector/mind-view.ts) and Memory Editor modal (static/js/inspector/memory-view.ts).

Current availability: mind-view.ts (lines 351-352) renders per-memory Suppress/Unblock buttons that pass (charName, entryId), but memory-view.ts (lines 300-310, 562) discards entryId and sends empty tags/keywords, wiping recall for every memory on the character.

Manual verification steps:
1. Open a character with multiple memories at world tick >= 5 and click Suppress on a single memory card in Inspector -> Mind.
   - expected: Only that memory shows the suppressed state while all other memories remain active; its until_tick reflects current_tick + duration.
2. Click Unblock on that suppressed memory (or inside the Memory Editor modal) while leaving a second suppressed memory untouched.
   - expected: Only the targeted memory is unblocked while unrelated suppressions remain intact.
